How to Legally Change Your Name in Kenya: A Practical Guide

Whether you're changing your name after marriage, correcting a spelling error, adopting a new identity for religious or personal reasons, or simply going by a name you feel better represents you, Kenyan law provides a clear path to make it official. Here's what you need to know before starting the process.

The Legal Basis

A name change in Kenya isn't just a matter of telling people to call you something different, it needs to be formally registered so that your new name is legally recognized on your ID, passport, and other official records. This process is governed primarily by the Registration of Documents Act (Cap. 285) and the Registration of Documents (Change of Name) Regulations.

The key legal instrument is the Deed Poll, which is the formal document in which you declare that you are abandoning your former name and adopting a new one, and that you require all persons to recognize you only by your new name going forward.

Who Can Apply

  • Adults (18 and above) can apply for a Deed Poll in their own right.
  • Minors aged 16–18 may consent to and sign their own Deed Poll, typically alongside a parent or guardian.
  • Children under 16 require a parent or legal guardian to sign on their behalf.
  • Children under 2 years old can usually have their name corrected directly on the birth register, without needing a full Deed Poll process.

The Step-by-Step Process

1. Draft the Deed Poll: The process begins with the preparation of a Deed Poll, which formally records your intention to abandon your former name and adopt a new one. The Deed Poll sets out your current name, proposed new name, and the declaration by which you undertake to use your new name going forward. The proposed name must comply with the applicable legal requirements and should, among other things, contain at least one forename and one surname. Names containing numbers, symbols, vulgar or offensive language, or titles that may falsely suggest an honour, rank or qualification are generally not permitted.

2. Sign Before a Witness and Swear a Statutory Declaration: Once the Deed Poll has been prepared, it must be properly executed in accordance with the applicable requirements. You will sign the Deed Poll in the presence of a witness and then execute a statutory declaration confirming your identity before a Commissioner for Oaths. Where the change of name involves adopting a spouse’s surname, the applicable consent and supporting documentation may also be required.

3. Register the Deed Poll The signed Deed Poll, together with supporting documents, is lodged with the Registrar of Documents.

4. Gazette Publication Once the Deed Poll has been registered, the name change is published in the Kenya Gazette as formal public notice. The publication provides an opportunity for any person with a legitimate objection to raise it within the prescribed period. Gazette publication is an important step in completing the process and formally recording the change of name.

5. Update Your Official Documents With your registered Deed Poll and Gazette Notice in hand, you can now apply to update your: National ID card, Passport, KRA PIN certificate, Bank records, academic certificates, and other institutional records as needed.

How Long Does It Take?

The process of changing your name may take one to three months, from preparation and registration of the Deed Poll to publication in the Kenya Gazette. Updating your identification documents and other official records may require additional time. Since processing timelines may vary depending on the relevant government offices, it is advisable to begin the process well in advance where the name change is required for purposes such as marriage, travel, employment, or other time-sensitive matters.

Costs

The process involves statutory charges payable to the relevant government agencies, in addition to professional fees for legal services. Statutory charges may include fees for registration, publication of the name change in the Kenya Gazette, and the statutory declaration. Our professional fees cover the preparation and execution of the necessary documents, guidance throughout the process, and related legal services. A clear breakdown of the applicable statutory charges and professional fees will be provided before the process begins.

Why Work With an Advocate

Although it is possible to undertake the name-change process independently, engaging an advocate can help ensure that the process is completed correctly and efficiently. An advocate can assist with the proper preparation and execution of the Deed Poll, ensure that the applicable identity, witnessing and attestation requirements are met, and guide you through registration and Gazette publication. Legal advice can also be particularly useful where the name change may affect property records, contracts, employment records, academic documents, financial accounts, or ongoing legal proceedings.
